summary: How the person reaches the Crew: the relay names them in its own frame, and the relay client stamps x-kiro-relay-user.
planPosition: x-kiro-relay-user-email and x-kiro-relay-user-name, and RFC 8187 for the name.
rule: The relay puts the verified Kiro user ID in the request head's user field, never in a header a client could send. The relay client sets x-kiro-relay-user on the request it hands to the Crew's web server, overwriting any value. The Crew honors the header only on requests from its relay client, in process or over a local channel authenticated with a secret the Crew holds, and strips it from everything else. On the local and Tailscale paths the Crew never honors it. On a personal Crew it honors it only when it names the owner. On a team Crew it takes the person as named. When the frame carries userEmail or userName, the relay client also sets x-kiro-relay-user-email, as given, and x-kiro-relay-user-name, RFC 8187 encoded in the UTF-8'' form even for an ASCII name, overwriting any value. Both are display only, and the Crew honors them only where it honors x-kiro-relay-user. A header it can't decode is ignored and the request is still served.

cases.name: local request carrying the header
cases.crewDoes: strips it and treats the request as not relayed

cases.name: personal Crew, a user who is not the owner
cases.crewDoes: refuses. The relay should never send this, so it is a second check

cases.name: relayed request with a non-ASCII name
relayed request with no name or email
client-sent name and email headers
cases.relayDoes: drops both with every other client-sent x-kiro header (dropped-client-headers.json), so they never reach the Crew

value: The person's stable Kiro user ID, never an email address or a display name.

names.x-kiro-relay-user-email: The person's email from the access token, display only, never compared.
names.x-kiro-relay-user-name: The person's name from the access token, RFC 8187 UTF-8'' form, display only, never compared.
